company_name: New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc.

sector_classification.gics_industry_group: Consumer Discretionary Distribution & Retail / Consumer Services
sector_classification.sub_classification: China private education services (test prep, non-academic tutoring, overseas consulting) with a diversified livestreaming e-commerce segment (East Buy)
sector_classification.notes: Straddles two GICS buckets in practice: core education/test-prep (Consumer Discretionary: Education Services) and East Buy's livestreaming e-commerce (Consumer Discretionary: Broadline Retail / Internet & Direct Marketing Retail). Index providers and screeners should tag EDU under Education Services as primary given it remains the majority of consolidated revenue and management identity.

overview: New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc. is a Beijing-headquartered, Cayman Islands-incorporated provider of private educational services in China, operating through a U.S.-listed ADR (NYSE: EDU) dual-listed in Hong Kong (9901.SEHK), with a May 31 fiscal year end. The company's historic core business of academic test-preparation and K-12 tutoring was forced into a dramatic restructuring by China's 2021 'double reduction' regulatory crackdown, and it has since rebuilt around four segments: educational services and test-preparation courses (now weighted toward adult/university test prep and non-academic K-12 tutoring), private label products and livestreaming e-commerce (East Buy, formerly Oriental Selection/Koolearn), overseas study consulting services, and educational materials and distribution. New Oriental operates through a VIE (variable interest entity) structure with PRC subsidiaries and contractual arrangements, as is standard for foreign-invested education providers in China, and reports its primary consolidated financial statements in U.S. dollars.

business_model.summary: Revenue is generated from tuition and course fees (largely prepaid, recognized as deferred revenue and amortized as courses are delivered), supplemented by East Buy's livestreaming e-commerce sales of private-label and third-party consumer products, overseas study consulting fees, and educational materials/book sales. The business transitioned from a K-9 academic tutoring-heavy mix pre-2021 to a more diversified mix of adult/university test prep, non-academic tutoring (STEAM, arts, sports), intelligent learning devices/systems, overseas consulting, and e-commerce. FY2026 revenue was ~US$5.66B, up 15.5% YoY, with operating margin expanding from 8.7% to 11.4% (non-GAAP operating margin 13.0%, up from 11.3%) as cost discipline and East Buy profitability improved.

revenue_streams.name: Educational Services & Test Preparation (adult/university test prep + non-academic K-12 tutoring + intelligent learning systems)
revenue_streams.notes: Domestic adult/university test prep grew ~14-29% YoY across FY2026 quarters; non-academic tutoring expanded to ~60 cities with >1,000,000 quarterly enrollments by 4Q FY2026; new educational business initiatives (non-academic tutoring, learning devices) grew 15-25% YoY through FY2026

revenue_streams.name: Overseas Study Consulting & Overseas Test Preparation
revenue_streams.notes: Low-single-digit growth (~1-7%) through FY2026, management flagged a 'continued slowdown in overseas businesses' in 1Q FY2026 commentary, reflecting weaker outbound study demand amid geopolitical/visa frictions

revenue_streams.name: East Buy (Private Label Products & Livestreaming E-Commerce)
revenue_streams.notes: GMV-driven business on Douyin (and other platforms) selling private-label food/health/household products under former-teacher hosts (e.g., Dong Yuhui/Dongfang Zhenxuan heritage); expanding Douyin vertical-account matrix (18 accounts by FY2026) and beginning offline experience stores via New Oriental learning centers in FY2027

revenue_streams.name: Educational Materials & Distribution
revenue_streams.notes: Smaller, stable legacy segment (books, content licensing)

business_model.customer_type: B2C (individual students and families) across K-12 non-academic, university/adult test-prep and overseas-study-consulting customers, plus mass-market B2C retail consumers for East Buy's e-commerce products
business_model.geographic_mix: Virtually all revenue generated within mainland China; reporting currency is USD (unusual for a PRC-based FPI, confirmed from filings' own statement headers), creating translation/convenience-rate dynamics versus RMB-denominated underlying operations
business_model.deferred_revenue_note: Deferred revenue (cash collected upfront from students) was US$2,242.9 million at FY2026 year-end, up 14.8% YoY, functioning as a leading indicator of forward revenue and enrollment momentum

main_competitors: TAL Education Group (TAL) - largest remaining academic/non-academic tutoring peer, comparable scale and similarly restructured post-double-reduction
Gaotu Techedu (GOTU) - online-focused tutoring/content peer, took a larger revenue hit from the crackdown
Yuanfudao and other private/unlisted K-12 tutoring platforms
China's state/public school system and informal tutoring (competing for non-academic/supplementary spend)
Douyin-native livestreaming hosts and MCNs (e.g., Li Jiaqi/'Lipstick King' on Taobao Live, Kuaishou hosts) and Alibaba's Taobao Live, Kuaishou, and JD for East Buy's e-commerce business
Overseas study consulting competitors: EIC Education, Vericant, and numerous boutique/local agencies
competitive_position.market_position: Among the two or three largest surviving private education brands in China post-double-reduction (alongside TAL and Gaotu), with particular strength in brand trust, teacher quality reputation, and a disproportionately large non-academic/adult test-prep franchise that was less exposed to the K-9 ban than peers. In livestreaming e-commerce, East Buy is a mid-tier but recognizable player riding the 'knowledge-based livestreaming' niche (former-teacher hosts selling curated, education-adjacent and quality-vetted private-label goods), competing against much larger platform-native ecosystems (Douyin's top MCNs, Taobao Live, Kuaishou) where East Buy does not control the distribution platform itself.

moat_factors.description: Four-decade-old 'New Oriental' brand is one of the most recognized education names in China, aiding trust-based enrollment even as the regulatory landscape and business mix shifted dramatically
National footprint of learning centers across dozens of cities supports an OMO (online-merge-offline) delivery model and now doubles as potential East Buy offline experience-store real estate

Demonstrated ability to navigate an existential regulatory shock (double reduction) and pivot business lines faster/more completely than some peers is itself a capability advantage, though it does not eliminate the risk of future adverse policy
Teacher talent pool and content/curriculum assets support both the education business and East Buy's distinctive 'knowledge-based livestreaming' differentiation

Limited classic network effects; students and e-commerce shoppers can switch to competitors with low friction, and East Buy does not own its distribution channel (dependent on Douyin and other third-party platforms)

weaknesses: No durable moat protects against adverse PRC regulatory action, which has already proven capable of eliminating a core revenue line overnight (2021)
East Buy's livestreaming e-commerce is platform-dependent (Douyin, etc.), intensely competitive, margin-thin, and subject to host/KOL concentration risk (reliance on specific presenter talent)

Overseas study consulting and overseas test-prep segments have shown sustained soft growth, suggesting secular/geopolitical headwinds (visa policy, de-risking sentiment) rather than purely cyclical softness
Reliance on a single dominant founder/chairman (Michael Yu) for strategic direction and brand association

growth_drivers: Continued expansion of non-academic K-12 tutoring (STEAM, arts, sports, life-skills) and intelligent learning systems/devices, which are not subject to the double-reduction academic-subject ban and have scaled to ~60 cities and over 1 million quarterly enrollments
Domestic adult and university test-preparation demand, which has consistently grown double digits (14-29% YoY across FY2026 quarters) and is largely insulated from K-9 regulation

AI integration across the OMO teaching system and into East Buy operations, explicitly cited by the CEO as 'a central organizational priority' for efficiency gains and product differentiation (e.g., AI-powered Intelligent Learning Device, Smart Study Solution launched 1Q FY2026)

East Buy's private-label product expansion, new Douyin vertical-account matrix (expanded from 7 to 18 channels across FY2026), membership-ecosystem development, and planned FY2027 offline experience stores leveraging New Oriental's existing real estate

'New Oriental Home' cross-selling customer-service platform (serving ~950,000+ families across ~69 cities by FY2026 year-end), designed to raise customer lifetime value and lower acquisition/marketing costs across business lines

Operating leverage/cost discipline: non-GAAP operating margin expanded 170bps in FY2026 (11.3% to 13.0%) via fixed-cost reduction and utilization improvements, with management guiding for continued efficiency gains in FY2027

Shareholder-return program (dividends + buybacks) as a demand lever for the stock, now in its second year with a disclosed ~US$300 million FY2027 dividend plan plus a US$200 million buyback authorization
Secular tailwind: China's large, education-focused household spending culture and continued demand for supplementary/non-academic enrichment and university-entrance-linked test prep

business.description: The 2021 'double reduction' policy eliminated for-profit K-9 academic tutoring virtually overnight, producing a ~US$1.2B net loss in FY2022 and forcing a full business-model pivot; PRC education policy remains unpredictable, and further restrictions (e.g., on non-academic tutoring, online education, data/content oversight, or livestreaming e-commerce) could again materially impair revenue with little warning

East Buy operates in a highly competitive, platform-dependent livestreaming e-commerce market against far larger and better-capitalized players (Douyin top MCNs, Taobao Live/Li Jiaqi, Kuaishou, JD); margins are thin and host/KOL-concentration and platform-algorithm dependency create volatility

business.risk: Customer/enrollment cyclicality tied to China's demographic and economic trends
business.description: China's declining birth rate and youth population could structurally shrink the addressable K-12 tutoring market over the long term

Sustained slow growth (flat to low-single-digit) in overseas test prep/consulting segments reflects weaker outbound study demand, potentially tied to geopolitical tension and visa/immigration frictions between China and Western destination countries

Michael Yu (Executive Chairman) is closely identified with the brand and strategy; management transition risk exists, though a CEO (Chenggang Zhou) and CFO (Stephen Zhihui Yang) run day-to-day operations

financial.description: Underlying operations are RMB-denominated while the company's primary reporting currency is USD; FY2027 revenue guidance is explicitly stated to be 'based on the current USD/RMB exchange rate, which is also subject to change,' so RMB depreciation would understate USD-reported growth

financial.risk: Capital allocation to illiquid/minority equity investments
financial.description: The balance sheet carries numerous minority equity-method and available-for-sale investments (education funds, Thaiwoo ski resort, Songtsam tourism, Sunlands, Mobvoi, etc.) that introduce fair-value volatility and capital tied up outside the core business

Periodic impairments on goodwill and long-term/equity investments (e.g., Beijing MaxEn fully impaired, Tibet Tianli, various available-for-sale positions) show that non-core investments have occasionally destroyed capital

regulatory.description: Beyond double reduction, ongoing PRC oversight of after-school tutoring content/hours/pricing, online education filings, and foreign-investment restrictions in education (including on kindergartens and compulsory-education-linked services) could tighten further

New Oriental conducts PRC operations through variable interest entities and contractual arrangements (not direct equity ownership) because PRC law restricts foreign ownership in education; China's Foreign Investment Law contains a catch-all provision that could someday classify VIE contractual arrangements as a restricted form of foreign investment, potentially forcing unwinding of the structure; ADS holders have no direct equity claim on the PRC operating entities

regulatory.risk: HFCAA / PCAOB audit-access and US-listed China delisting risk
regulatory.description: The Holding Foreign Companies Accountable Act requires delisting of PRC issuers whose auditors the PCAOB cannot inspect for three consecutive years; the 2022 US-China agreement restored PCAOB inspection access and reduced near-term delisting risk, but the arrangement remains politically contingent and could be revoked or tightened amid renewed US-China tension, and EDU's dual Hong Kong listing (9901.SEHK, fungible with the NYSE ADS) provides a partial hedge/contingency
Online education and livestreaming content are subject to PRC internet-content, data-security, and licensing rules; compliance failures could trigger platform shutdowns or fines

macro.risk: China consumer spending and macro slowdown
macro.description: Both education discretionary spend and East Buy's consumer-retail demand are sensitive to Chinese household income growth, property-market wealth effects, and overall consumer confidence

Broader bilateral friction (tariffs, export controls, capital-markets rhetoric) creates headline risk for all US-listed China ADRs regardless of company-specific fundamentals, and could affect overseas-study demand and investor sentiment/valuation multiples
RMB depreciation against the USD mechanically reduces USD-reported revenue and guidance ranges even when underlying RMB business performance is stable or improving

execution.risk: Integration and scaling of new business lines
execution.description: Non-academic tutoring, intelligent learning devices, and East Buy's offline-store expansion (planned FY2027) are relatively new initiatives requiring successful scaling, capital allocation discipline, and operational execution distinct from the legacy core-education playbook
4Q FY2026 results noted 'one-time costs and expenses arising from... internal management restructuring,' indicating ongoing organizational change that could recur and pressure near-term margins

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's private education/tutoring industry has stabilized post-double-reduction around non-academic enrichment, adult/university test prep, and vocational/professional training, which policymakers have generally tolerated or encouraged (distinct from the banned for-profit K-9 academic subject tutoring). China's livestreaming e-commerce market continues to grow rapidly (projected to reach several trillion RMB in GMV by 2026), though competition among Douyin, Taobao Live, and Kuaishou ecosystems is intensifying.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - education spending in China is relatively resilient/counter-cyclical for test-prep-driven demand (exam-linked, not discretionary luxury), but East Buy's retail e-commerce segment and overseas study consulting are more sensitive to consumer discretionary spending cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity (asset-light, cash-rich balance sheet with term deposits/short-term investments); indirect sensitivity via Chinese consumer confidence and property-market wealth effects
macro_factors.currency_exposure: High - RMB-denominated operations reported in USD; FY2027 guidance explicitly flagged as FX-rate-dependent
key_input_costs: Private-label product sourcing costs for East Buy
macro_factors.regulatory_environment_trend: Stabilizing but not fully de-risked; the most severe shock (double reduction) is several years in the past and the surviving business mix was deliberately restructured to reduce exposure to the banned category, but PRC education and internet-content policy remains an active, evolving area

recent_developments.event: Reported Q4 FY2026 revenue of US$1,529.5M (+23.0% YoY) and FY2026 full-year revenue of US$5,661.3M (+15.5% YoY); non-GAAP operating margin expanded to 13.0% for FY2026 from 11.3% in FY2025; issued FY2027 revenue guidance of US$6,453.9M-US$6,680.3M (+14% to +18% YoY)
Announced FY2027 shareholder return plan: ~US$300 million ordinary cash dividend (two installments, December 2026 and June 2027) plus a new US$200 million share repurchase authorization
Completed FY2026 US$300 million buyback program announced October 2025 (~51.5 million shares repurchased for ~US$274.0 million as of July 2026)

Q3 FY2026 revenue of US$1,417.3M (+19.8% YoY), operating income +44.8% YoY, non-GAAP operating margin of 14.3% (up 230bps YoY); East Buy expanded Douyin vertical-account matrix with new channels (East Buy Home, Fruit & Vegetables, Nutrition & Health)
New Oriental scheduled to report Q1 FY2027 results before market open
EDU shares crossed above their 200-day moving average, a technical signal noted by market trackers amid broader share-price recovery

Sell-side sentiment improved through 2026: Goldman Sachs upgraded EDU from Neutral to Buy (June 2026, PT $65), Macquarie upgraded from Underperform to Neutral (PT raised to $56.50 from $49, citing increased shareholder returns), and BofA raised its price target to $73.20 from $71.30 (Buy); consensus rating is Buy with an average 12-month price target near $73.6

Launched AI-powered Intelligent Learning Device and Smart Study Solution; management flagged a 'continued slowdown' in overseas test-prep/consulting businesses even as domestic adult/university test prep and new educational initiatives grew double digits; announced FY2026 ordinary dividend (US$0.12/common share, ~US$190M aggregate) and US$300M buyback as first implementation of the new three-year shareholder return plan
Board adopted a three-year shareholder return plan committing no less than 50% of the prior fiscal year's net income attributable to New Oriental to dividends and/or buybacks, commencing FY2026

Declared a special cash dividend of US$0.06 per common share (US$0.6/ADS), approximately US$100 million aggregate - New Oriental's first dividend as a public company, signaling the transition to a more mature, cash-return-oriented capital allocation stance post-restructuring

items.notes: Represents 14% to 18% YoY growth; management describes the forecast as 'current and preliminary,' subject to change, and explicitly based on the prevailing USD/RMB exchange rate, which is also subject to change

items.target: ~US$300 million aggregate, paid in two installments (December 2026 and June 2027)
items.vs_prior: raised vs FY2026 (~US$190 million aggregate ordinary dividend)
items.notes: Implements the three-year shareholder return plan (no less than 50% of prior-year net income attributable to New Oriental returned via dividends/buybacks); exact per-share/per-ADS amount to be announced by the board in due course

items.target: Up to US$200 million of ADSs or common shares over 12 months following board approval
items.notes: To be funded from existing cash balance; terms/size subject to periodic board review

items.target: No specific numeric target disclosed; qualitative guidance for continued margin expansion via fixed-cost reduction and operational efficiency
items.vs_prior: maintained direction (expansion), building on FY2026's 170bp improvement (11.3% to 13.0%)
items.notes: CFO commentary: 'we will continue to execute our cost and efficiency initiatives across key business lines in the coming new fiscal year... aim to steadily reduce fixed costs, drive further operational efficiencies'

guidance.management_commentary: Executive Chairman Michael Yu emphasized the 'soundness of our core education strategy' and highlighted New Oriental Home (cross-selling/customer-retention platform now serving ~950,000 families across 69 cities) as a structural driver of lower acquisition costs and higher customer lifetime value. CEO Chenggang Zhou stressed 'disciplined capacity expansion' balancing growth with efficiency, deepening AI integration across the OMO teaching system, and outlined East Buy's FY2027 priorities: offline experience stores via New Oriental learning centers, accelerated private-label development, refined membership operations, and improved supply-chain efficiency. CFO Stephen Zhihui Yang flagged one-time costs from internal management restructuring in 4Q FY2026 but reaffirmed confidence in continued non-GAAP margin expansion into FY2027.

bull_case: Demonstrated resilience and successful reinvention after an existential regulatory shock (2021 double reduction), with FY2026 revenue (~US$5.66B) now well above pre-crackdown levels and margins expanding (non-GAAP operating margin 13.0%, +170bps YoY), proving management's ability to navigate China's regulatory environment

Diversified, de-risked revenue base relative to 2021: non-academic tutoring, adult/university test prep, intelligent learning devices, and East Buy e-commerce are all largely outside the banned for-profit K-9 academic tutoring category, reducing (though not eliminating) single-policy tail risk

New, maturing capital-return program (dividends since 2024, buybacks, three-year 50%-of-net-income return commitment, ~US$300M FY2027 dividend plan) signals confidence in sustainable free cash flow and provides a valuation floor/yield support atypical of past-generation China ADRs

AI integration across OMO teaching and East Buy operations, plus the 'New Oriental Home' cross-sell platform, could structurally lower customer acquisition costs and raise lifetime value, supporting durable margin expansion

Improving sell-side sentiment in 2026 (Goldman Sachs upgrade to Buy, Macquarie upgrade to Neutral, BofA price-target increase) with consensus Buy rating and meaningful implied upside to the ~$73.6 average 12-month price target
bear_case: Regulatory risk is structurally unresolved: the 2021 double-reduction episode proved PRC policy can eliminate a core revenue line with little warning, and non-academic tutoring, online education, or livestreaming e-commerce could face fresh restrictions at any time

East Buy operates in a brutally competitive, platform-dependent livestreaming e-commerce market against far larger players (Douyin's top MCNs, Taobao Live/Li Jiaqi, Kuaishou), with thin margins and reliance on specific host talent and third-party platform algorithms outside the company's control

VIE/contractual-arrangement structure means ADS holders have no direct equity claim on the PRC operating entities; evolving PRC Foreign Investment Law interpretation could, in a worst case, force unwinding of these arrangements

Overseas study consulting/test-prep segments show sustained soft growth, suggesting a secular (geopolitical, visa-policy-driven) rather than purely cyclical headwind to a historically important growth segment

US-listed China ADRs remain exposed to headline/geopolitical risk (HFCAA/PCAOB audit-access arrangements are politically contingent and could be revisited) and to RMB/USD currency translation, both of which can move the stock independent of underlying PRC-RMB business fundamentals
